level3:1.caption: The 5-Levels of Leadership chart (Level 1 CC-Member/Sower through Level 5 Coordinator), the model students must be able to draw from memory.
level3:1.alt: Chart with five columns showing the five levels of leadership: Level 1 CC-Member/Sower, Level 2 CC-Starter/Planter, Level 3 CC-Starts a Second CC/Multiplier, Level 4 Lead CCs to Reach City/Trainer, and Level 5 Launch CCs to a Second City/Coordinator, each with a progression arrow.

level3:10.caption: Church Mapping model: the generational map of a church network with health symbols inside each circle, used to track spread and health.
level3:10.alt: Church map showing two first-generation church circles, two second-generation church circles, and one third-generation dashed House of Peace circle, with arrows between generations and health-activity symbols inside each circle.

level3:3.caption: The complete Life Cycle of Movement chart with the sweet-spot shaded box and symbol key, the central model of Lesson 3.
level3:3.alt: Chart of the movement lifecycle showing phases Phase 0-1, Movement, Formalization, and Institutionalization, with a red shaded box marking the sweet spot, plus a symbol key for new believers, priesthood, house church starts, generations, gifted leaders, buildings, and seminary.

level3:3.caption: Boat-and-wind illustration for Lesson 3: the sailboat represents experiencing the Spirit's movement toward the X (end vision).
level3:3.alt: Small sailboat illustration with wind streams blowing from behind toward a blue arrow marked with an X, representing the Spirit moving the movement toward its destination.

level3:4.caption: The Leadership Circle: the 4G+ Entry-Gospel-Disciple-Church cycle with the eight T symbols that students draw in the circle.
level3:4.alt: Leadership Circle diagram: a red circular arrow around 4G+ with the four fields Entry, Gospel, Disciple, and Church, plus the eight T symbols and labels for Timing, Targets, Tools, Team, Training, Tracking, Troubleshoot, and Treasure.

level3:5.caption: The Timing priorities chart: how a Level 3 leader invests weekly time across Missions, Family, and Tent-Making.
level3:5.alt: Priorities schedule chart with three sections: Missions 16 hours total (personal time with Jesus, fellowship with 3 Timothies, training levels), Family 31 hours total, and Tent-Making 44 hours total, with daily and weekly time allocations.

level3:6.caption: The End-Vision Diagram: the blue Great Commission arrow aimed at the Vision target with five backward-planned milestones.
level3:6.alt: End-Vision diagram: a blue arrow labeled GREAT COMMMISSION pointing into a red VISION target bull's-eye, with five numbered backward-planned milestone lines numbered 1 to 5 above and below.

level3:8.caption: The Jesus 1-3-9 multiplication diagram: one leader invests in three, who each invest in three, growing to 40 people.
level3:8.alt: Stick-figure multiplication diagram showing one person investing in three people, each of those three investing in three more, expanding to forty people total, illustrating the Jesus 1-3-9 model.

level3:8.caption: Vision-casting illustration 1: the boat (team) follows the straight dotted line of milestones to the X (end vision).
level3:8.alt: Vision-casting illustration 1: a small boat with a straight dotted line leading to an X marked on a gray landmass, representing the mission to reach the end-vision destination by milestones.

level3:8.caption: Vision-casting illustration 2: storms blow the boat off course; sailors compare map to stars and compass to chart a new course.
level3:8.alt: Vision-casting illustration 2: a small boat with a dotted line toward an X on a landmass, representing storms blowing the team off course and the need to seek God's direction and chart a new course.

level3:8.caption: Vision-casting illustration 3: the boat curves around an outcropping of rocks, illustrating adjusting goals to avoid obstacles.
level3:8.alt: Vision-casting illustration 3: a small boat with a curved dotted line going around a dark outcropping of rocks toward an X, representing adjusting goals to go around obstacles instead of crashing into them.

level3:8.caption: The APE/PT tension diagram: PTs pull new believers to slow down and grow up while APEs push them to go out and labor, creating healthy tension.
level3:8.alt: Diagram with a vertical axis labeled PT's (arrow up) and a horizontal axis labeled APE's (arrow forward), with a red diagonal arrow labeled TENSION between them, showing the balance of growing up and going out.
